newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Pyongyang vows "merciless retaliation" over sub.
newsitem.headline: Pyongyang vows "merciless retaliation" over sub.

text.p: North Korea threatened "merciless retaliation" against South Korea on Saturday over the deaths of its soldiers who came ashore from a submarine last month.

"Our retaliation will be merciless," the official Korea Central News Agency said. "Blood should be paid for blood," the agency said in the most harshly-worded threat so far over the submarine incident.
Out of 26 men who landed, 22 have either been killed by Southern troops or found dead. One has been captured alive and the hunt is on for three others.
Pyongyang has demanded the return of the submarine, found grounded on rocks on September 18, along with the dead crew and survivors.

On Wednesday Pyongyang army officers warned of "serious consequences" over the incident in a border meeting with representatives of the U.S.-led United Nations Command that monitors the ceasefire that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.

"The South Korean puppets should be held responsible wholly for any form of our retaliation," KCNA said on Saturday. "We will make them pay for their crimes a thousandfold by just means and method, when an occasion comes."
